newsitem.title: UK: LME copper little changed late, aluminium firmer.
newsitem.headline: LME copper little changed late, aluminium firmer.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) three months copper was little changed from the kerb in late Thursday inter-office activity as the market awaited Friday LME warehouse stocks data. Copper had fluctuated widely on Thursday as the market attempted to consolidate after the past few weeks' gains. It ended the kerb at $2,212 per tonne, down $3 from Wednesday, and was bid at $2,213 at 1900 GMT when Comex closed. Friday's stocks data is expected to give the market its next direction, with interest centred on how far an overall decline may be bottoming out and on what volumes may flow in to Singapore.
"Should further increases in Singapore stocks be seen this could provide the impetus for an aggressive bear raid..." brokerage Rudolf Wolff said in its Evening Metal Report.
But it added that "we feel that significant increases over a prolonged period would be required for the risk of upside spikes to be alleviated".
The market will also watch Hamburg and Long Beach to see if there is an end to the recent drawdowns.
Aluminium twice dipped to $1,500 during the day but the downside found good buying interest and last kerb business was at $1,504, down just $4 a tonne from Wednesday.
Aluminium was then bid firmer at $1,518 by the hour of the Comex close after buyers reappeared.
